baseline.note: Language-dominated: all clustering methods achieve 93-100% language purity but only 17-58% legal-area purity

best_legal_area_purity.note: At cost of 1.0 language purity — clusters are monolingual sub-groups

hierarchy_consistency.note: Hierarchy splits cleanly but follows language boundaries, not legal doctrine

section_experiment.note: Sachverhalt/Dispositiv achieve ratio > 0.5 but primarily via language de-correlation, not legal signal gain. Erwägungen (legal reasoning) is MORE language-dominated (0.92) than full_text (0.89)

critical_finding: All tested representations are dominated by language (DE/FR/IT), not legal content. The fractal hierarchy is consistent (NMI 0.79-0.91) but splits follow language boundaries. The product question 'do structured sections improve legal coherence?' is answered: only for facts/outcome (marginally), not for reasoning. Legal-distance lane must produce legal-specific embeddings before fractal-map can produce a law map rather than a language map.
